summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, diverticulosis, and recent UTI treated with ciprofloxacin presented with 24 hours of watery diarrhea and crampy abdominal pain after eating out, with no fever or vomiting. Symptoms had resolved by the time of evaluation. She was hemodynamically stable with no leukocytosis. A CT scan ruled out diverticulitis, and repeat urinalysis was negative, confirming resolution of her prior UTI. Stool studies were negative for C. difficile, Salmonella, Shigella, and Campylobacter. Given symptom resolution and reassuring workup, she was observed for 24 hours and discharged home with a diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis. Chronic thrombocytopenia was noted but stable, with outpatient follow-up planned. No antibiotics were prescribed.
